newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Chinese foreign minister to visit Lisbon for talks.
newsitem.headline: Chinese foreign minister to visit Lisbon for talks.

text.p: Chinese Foreign Minister Qian Qichen arrives in Lisbon on Saturday for talks to centre on a handover of power in the Portuguese administered territory of Macau, foreign ministry officials said.
The island of Macau, where the Portuguese have been present since the 16th century, is due to be returned formally to Chinese rule on midnight on December 31, 1999.
The process has so far been free of the tensions that have surrounded the return of British-ruled Hong Kong to Chinese control, which is due to take place on June 30, 1997.
"Obviously, there are differences to be resolved but overall the move towards the transition is going well," a Portuguese foreign ministry spokesman said.
Officials said that Portugal was pressing for guarantees on human rights after it withdraws from Macau, with the issue of the death penalty a case in point.
Portugal abolished the death penalty more than 100 years ago but it is still regularly used in China.
Qichen, who visited Portugal's former African colonies of Sao Tome and Principe and Cape Verde on his way to Lisbon, begins the official part of his trip on Monday.

The planned two and a half hours of talks with Foreign Minister Jaime Gama will also cover the United Nations Security Council where Portugal has just begun a two-year stint as a non-permanent member, officials said.
His visit comes just a month before Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio leaves for a two-week trip to Macau and China on February 17.
